results.title: Incredible Part of Nepali Life
results.text:
This is a large temple dedicated to Shiva and is the temple where the dead are cremated.  I hired a tour guide who spoke great English and provided me with quite a detailed tour.  I ended up paying him USD $20.  Might be high, but he was good.  

Anyway, the temple itself is in a sprawling complex that spans the highly polluted Bagmati river.  Along the river, the dead are cremated and their ashes pushed into the river.  It is apparently the holiest river in all of Hindu.  

From across the river, you can watch the preparation and cleaning of the bodies, their movement to the cremation stands, and the cremation.  It's quite a spectacle.  You can also wander the grounds and see the Brahmans and other holymen/women.  

If I recall, the entrance fee for foreigners was NRps 500.

results.title: The Great Hindu faith Place
results.text: Pashupatinath is the most important Hindu Temple in Nepal. It is situated 5 km east of Kathmandu on the banks of the holy Bagmati River. This is the temple of Lord Shiva one of three major gods in Hinduism. This temple has two tiered golden roof and silver doors. Although only Hindus are allowed inside the main temple, visitors can clearly see the temple and the activities performed in the temple premises from the eastern bank of the Bagmati River. The other attraction of visiting this temple is cremation death human body. On the bank of Bagmati River there are many cremation spots. On those spot there is almost always a cremation going on. While walking around Pashupatinath you will meet many devotees and sadhus (wandering Hindu holy men). This temple was listed in the UNESCO’s World heritage monument list in 1979.

results.title: Fascinating
results.text: Fascinating place and very touching to see the cremating places. Especially if you've also been to Varanasi in India, since the two places are so very different.

results.title: Amazed!
results.text:
It is quite amazing to me to see monkeys walk around the temple and pass human beings without so much as a glance (though we were staring at them all goggle-eyed). Small monkeys, big monkeys, HUGE monkeys... just walking around like it's the most normal thing in the world! And i guess it is, for them! :) 
I got to the temple in the evening, after dark, and found it extremely peaceful, with more animals than human beings and loved the experience!

results.title: Never a dull moment
results.text: I have traveled to Nepal many times and have visted Pashupatinath on every trip. It is actually a very large park with monkeys, sadhus and public cremations. I think it's a must see place for anyone traveling to Nepal if you're in the Kathmandu area. I personally find the cremations fascinating and if you ask around you can find a sadhu who will perform penis yoga for a fee. My only advice would be to stay clear of the younger men who will approach you wanted to be your tour guide. They have a lot of information to offer but also view tourists as "marks" as they divide up based on the various languages visitors speak. If you go to Pilgrims Bookstore you migh be better off getting a book instead of a guide.

results.title: This was a new experience...
results.text:
...I thought I know a lot and I am able to capture different cultural behaviour - after visiting this place I made a big steo forward. 
I was so fascinated about this place about the people, cultural differences, monkeys....etc.

results.title: Cremations and monkeys
results.text: This temple is right on the river and chances are there will be a cremation going on while you are there, which is a fascinating though somber sight. There are also masses of monkeys that are so close you can pet (though I wouldn't!). This was a big plus for me, but might be a big turnoff for some.

results.title: Interesting experience but could have been alerted...
results.text: An interesting experience but guides could have pre-alert tourists on the possibility of bumping into ongoing ceremony where dead body are being carried along the path to be cremated.  Non-Hindus, maybe Asians who are superstitious may find this to be a taboo  Just keep your ears opened for "sea-shell horn" blowing and step aside - this is the signs of opening the path as they carry the dead body to the burning place.

results.title: Totally Recommended!
results.text: I was in the temple 3 times during  my trip to Nepal! But of course being a Shiva devotee i am a little bit biased and would naturally recommend Pashupatinath temple to just about anyone.But the first time i stepped into this wonderful place i was overwhelmed with emotions and it was something everyone should experience at least once in their life.But of course Non Hindus are not allowed into the main temples but once can always sit by the Bagmati River and get a different feel of the whole surrounding.Anyhow the first day i went bit too late thats like 8 am and its already crowded!So the 2nd day i went around 6 am and that was better as you can do your pooja at your own pace and maybe get a look at Lord Pashupati a while longer and then you can join the bhajan group and sing along Shiva devotional songs..All in all i would recommend this place again and again..Oh yea stay away from sadhus if you can! and you dont need a guide to go around the temple..just be cautious of your surroundings and take care of your belongings..the usual precautionary steps which applies everywhere..

results.title: Holiest place for Hindus
results.text: This temple is one of the oldest and the holiest place for Hindus. Nepal is the only Hindu country in the World not India as India is secular not Hindu! Lord Shiva took a temporary abode here till found by the Gods again. The main temple is open to Hindus only all other faith have to stay on the back side next to the cremation grounds. If you are Hindu then use a guide who can tell you the history of the temple and explain the meaning of all the writings and idols. It was a divine experience for us. If you are looking to buy the holy bead "Rudraksha" then go to one of main shops. Its all authentic but expensive so bargain.
